Urea.name: Urea
Urea.management_note: Apply in split doses (e.g. basal + vegetative topdressing) to minimize leaching and ammonia volatilization. Avoid broad application during mature/ripening stage.

DAP.name: Di-Ammonium Phosphate (DAP)
DAP.management_note: Primarily applied at basal / early planting stage. Insoluble P fixates in soil; localized band placement near root zone is recommended.

MOP.name: Muriate of Potash (MOP / Potassium Chloride)
MOP.management_note: Essential for osmotic regulation, enzymatic activation, and drought tolerance. In light/sandy soils, apply in splits with Nitrogen.

SSP.name: Single Super Phosphate (SSP)
SSP.management_note: Ideal basal phosphorus source especially for sulfur-demanding crops (oilseeds, pulses) and calcium-deficient soils.

NPK_19_19_19.name: NPK 19-19-19 (Water Soluble Complex)
NPK_19_19_19.management_note: 100% water soluble; suitable for fertigation or corrective foliar spray during active vegetative and flowering stages.

yield_multi_factors: Crop cultivar/hybrid genetics and seed viability
Planting density and canopy spatial geometry
Soil physical structure, texture, and organic matter content
Soil pH and secondary/micronutrient balance (Zn, Fe, B, S)
Weed, pest, and fungal disease pressure
Ambient temperature, solar radiation, and extreme weather events
agronomic_principles.yield_warning: High fertilizer dosage does NOT guarantee high yield. Yield is governed by Liebig's Law of the Minimum, where growth is constrained by the scarcest resource (e.g. water, micronutrients, or pest control), not by the total amount of nutrients added.
